status: pre-implementation diagnostic protocol; no runtime adoption
cases: all 40 unchanged supplied question occurrences; known development cases, not held out
arm: B1: BM25 over original full source-unit text with original query tokens only; no expansion, heading fields, card summaries, benefit-specific weighting or filtering.
tokenisation: Use the approved corpusTokens normalisation/regex, retaining repeated document tokens for term frequencies and length. Query tokens are the same unique scaffold-filtered tokens retained in A.
score: Sum ln(1 + (N - df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5)) * (tf * (k1 + 1)) / (tf + k1 * (1 - b + b * dl/avgdl)) for original query terms; ties use ascending canonical ordinal. N, df and avgdl cover all source-unit records, including uncertain candidates.
baseline: Reuse the hash-bound A result whose 40 candidate orders were checked against the approved engine; independently reconstruct A from the corpus during this probe.
measures: Per-case candidate-location overlap with the earlier incomplete source-candidate register, explicitly not relevance or answer accuracy.
Top16 whole-source bytes and candidate identity changes.
Change in candidate lengths, all gains and losses, and status of every selected unit.
boundaries: No new source, summary generation, provider call or live engine change.
No wrong-heading metadata is used. This isolates terminology before structural/summary card experiments.
Source-candidate locations are incomplete review leads, not an exhaustive correct-answer set.
Retain every case, regressions and null outcomes. No thresholds or weights tuned after observing results.
No claim of full-unit dependency closure or answerability from ranking alone.
This later development experiment is motivated by the observed long-fragment failure; it is not held out.
Freeze this protocol in Git before implementation and execution. Do not tune parameters after seeing the results.
Any positive candidate overlap remains a lead for independent relevance review, not grounds for changing production ranking.
